title: Introduce lint-flight-controller and release-sentinel to stabilize presubmit lanes and release windows
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Stabilize presubmit lint routing and add a release sentinel to reduce noisy releases; no user-facing API changes.
description: Context and motivation: Our presubmit lanes have grown noisy and fragile as we split linting across multiple runtime profiles. This caused frequent fast-fail merges and spurious release automation triggers during peak traffic. This PR introduces a lightweight 'lint flight controller' that routes lint jobs to staged lanes based on path-awareness and an adaptive backoff, and a 'release sentinel' service that enforces quiet windows and validates release preconditions before the automated release bridge runs. Goals: 1) reduce CI flakiness and developer churn by routing low-risk lint jobs to fast lanes, 2) prevent accidental release churn by gating automated releases behind a short, deterministic sentinel check, 3) centralize a few small presubmit heuristics so they can be tuned without editing many workflow files. What changed (high-level): Added a small Go controller (scripts/ci/flight_controller.go) that evaluates changed paths and assigns presubmit lint shards to fast/slow lanes; added a Python release sentinel (tools/release/sentinel.py) that queries CI state, open incident flags, and Linear gates before allowing the release pipeline to continue; refactored .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml to call the controller via a remote HTTP hook or local binary; updated docs and operator runbook; small helper Dockerfile.ci and Makefile targets. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1724) - [x] Unit + integration tests for controller - [x] E2E smoke for sentinel - [x] Update operator docs - [x] Coordinated rollout with Platform team Changes summary / commits: commit 1: feat(ci): add lint flight controller skeleton and router commit 2: refactor(ci): split presubmit lanes and call controller hook commit 3: feat(release): add release sentinel and gating API commit 4: test(ci): add unit tests for routing logic and sentinel mocks commit 5: docs: add runbook and rollout notes Files touched (illustrative): .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml (refactor to use controller hook), scripts/ci/flight_controller.go (new), tools/release/sentinel.py (new), Dockerfile.ci (new target), docs/ci/release-sentinel.md (new), docs/ci/flight-controller.md (new), Makefile (ci targets), scripts/ci/runner_helper.sh (small changes), examples/presubmit-config.yaml (tuning presets). Small illustrative diff snippet: scripts/ci/flight_controller.go: +120 LOC added, implements path-hash bucketing and lane decision API; tools/release/sentinel.py: +180 LOC, simple HTTP server + Linear check. Rollout plan: - Deploy controller binary to ephemeral runner images and enable remote hook on a small subset of repos (start with redwood/*) - Monitor presubmit latency and misroute rate for 48h - Flip default routing after 72h if error rate <0.5% - Enable release sentinel in release pipeline for a 1-week canary (non-blocking logging mode first, then blocking), coordinate with on-call SRE for early mornings. Runtime considerations: Controller is intentionally small and stateless; decisions are deterministic based on changed paths + config. Sentinel persists only short-lived guard records in GCS with TTL to support retries. Backwards compatibility: Workflows fall back to previous behavior if controller or sentinel time out (default path = slow-lane, release sentinel times out -> block and notify).
